parts.visual:
A founder launches a product and sends a generic press release to 500 journalists at info@news.com. Nobody replies. Another founder finds out that a specific journalist at TechCrunch loves writing about AI in healthcare. The founder sends them a direct, exclusive Twitter message with a controversial angle. The journalist writes the story. The startup gets 50,000 users in a day.

The PR Machine:
1. The Exclusive: Journalists are competing for clicks. If you send the same story to everyone, no one cares. If you offer a top-tier journalist an 'Exclusive' (promising no other magazine will get the story until they publish), they are highly incentivized to write it.
2. The 'Funding Announcement' Loophole: Tech blogs love writing about money. A startup can use a $5 Million seed round announcement as an excuse to get a massive article written about their actual product.
parts.audio: Journalists do not exist to provide free advertising for your app. They exist to tell interesting stories to their readers. If your pitch is 'We made an app', you go to the spam folder. If your pitch is 'We are destroying a 100-year-old monopoly', you get the front page.

questions.question: What does it mean to offer a journalist an 'Embargo'?
options: Giving them all the secret information (product launch details, funding numbers) a week early so they have time to write a great article, under the strict legal promise that they will not publish it until a specific date and time.
questions.correct_answer: Giving them all the secret information (product launch details, funding numbers) a week early so they have time to write a great article, under the strict legal promise that they will not publish it until a specific date and time.
questions.explanation: Embargoes allow for coordinated, massive launch days.

questions.question: Listen to the PR agency director. Why do startups hire $10,000/month PR firms?
questions.tts_text: We don't write better emails than the founders. We are paid because we have the personal cell phone numbers of the top 20 journalists at the New York Times and TechCrunch. We bypass the inbox and go straight to the editor.
options: The Rolodex. PR is entirely based on relationships and trust. A journalist ignores emails from unknown founders, but will open an email from a PR agent who has brought them great stories for the last 5 years.
Because they know how to code.
questions.correct_answer: The Rolodex. PR is entirely based on relationships and trust. A journalist ignores emails from unknown founders, but will open an email from a PR agent who has brought them great stories for the last 5 years.
questions.explanation: In PR, who you know is more important than what you write.

questions.question: A startup pays a PR firm $15,000, gets a massive article in TechCrunch, gets 10,000 new users that day... and then next week traffic drops to zero. Why?
options: The PR Spike Fallacy. Press is a steroid injection, not a business model. A massive article will cause a huge 48-hour spike in traffic, but if the product has bad retention, all those users will churn. PR cannot fix a bad product.
questions.correct_answer: The PR Spike Fallacy. Press is a steroid injection, not a business model. A massive article will cause a huge 48-hour spike in traffic, but if the product has bad retention, all those users will churn. PR cannot fix a bad product.
questions.explanation: A megaphone is useless if you have nothing to say.

questions.question: Why is 'Newsjacking' an effective startup PR strategy?
options: Injecting your company into a massive breaking news story. If a giant bank is hacked, a cybersecurity startup immediately emails journalists offering the CEO as an 'expert commentator' on why the hack happened, getting their brand free national television exposure.
questions.correct_answer: Injecting your company into a massive breaking news story. If a giant bank is hacked, a cybersecurity startup immediately emails journalists offering the CEO as an 'expert commentator' on why the hack happened, getting their brand free national television exposure.
questions.explanation: Ride the wave of existing attention.
